P1.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation
P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
P1.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

P2.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation

E0.variant: Quiet Bilateral Standing — no-step orientation teaching task
E0.effort_load: Bodyweight, minimal effort.2s settle,2s comfortable quiet standing,6s reset. Arms relaxed, knees unlocked; no deliberate lowering, travel or technical knee target.
E0.notes: This observes simple orientation/stop-cue participation only. No travel, marching or upright-running pass follows.

E1.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation
E1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
E1.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

S1.variant: Tempo Bodyweight Squat — comfortable bilateral stance/range
S1.effort_load: Bodyweight only;3s lower/1s gentle pause/1s stand, at least5 controlled reps in reserve. Keep the documented OR-01 range when applicable.

S2.variant: Bodyweight Hip Hinge Good Morning — arms crossed at chest
S2.effort_load: Bodyweight;3s hips back/1s stand, at least5 good reps in reserve. Retain the actual comfortable range and arm position.

S3.variant: Incline Push-Up — individually verified stable high support
S3.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s press, at least5 good reps in reserve.90cm is a planning reference only; retain the qualified actual support height and foot position or select a suitable high surface for instruction.
S3.notes: Record actual support height. Older age does not lower the surface or add repetitions.

S4.variant: Ring/TRX Row — verified anchors, about70-degree body angle to floor
S4.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s pull, at least5 good reps in reserve; record actual angle.

S5.variant: 90/90 Breathing with Reach — lower-leg-supported-bilateral-reach
S5.effort_load: Very low; comfortable2s in/3s out, no holds or forced depth; calves/heels fully supported, no heel pull/hip lift.

P1.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation
P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
P1.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

P2.variant: Short Corridor Walk — ordinary walking orientation
P2.effort_load: Bodyweight, ordinary conversational walking about2/10. Recognize the assigned markers and exit; no jog, forced technical thigh height, abrupt terminal plant or timed redirect.
P2.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate18s; separate outside walking return20s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations.

E0.effort_load: Bodyweight, ordinary conversational walking about2/10. Recognize the assigned markers and exit; no jog, forced technical thigh height, abrupt terminal plant or timed redirect.

E1.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate20s; separate outside walking return20s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations.

S1.variant: Tempo Bodyweight Squat — comfortable bilateral stance/range
S1.effort_load: Bodyweight only;3s lower/1s gentle pause/1s stand, at least5 controlled reps in reserve. Keep the documented OR-01 range when applicable.

S2.variant: Bodyweight Hip Hinge Good Morning — arms crossed at chest
S2.effort_load: Bodyweight;3s hips back/1s stand, at least5 good reps in reserve. Retain the actual comfortable range and arm position.

S3.variant: Incline Push-Up — individually verified stable high support
S3.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s press, at least5 good reps in reserve.90cm is a planning reference only; retain the qualified actual support height and foot position or select a suitable high surface for instruction.
S3.notes: Record actual support height. Older age does not lower the surface or add repetitions.

S4.variant: Ring/TRX Row — verified anchors, about70-degree body angle to floor
S4.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s pull, at least5 good reps in reserve; record actual angle.

S5.effort_load: Very low; comfortable2s in/3s out, no holds or forced depth; calves/heels fully supported, no heel pull/hip lift.

P1.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

P2.variant: Short Corridor Walk — ordinary walking orientation
P2.effort_load: Bodyweight, ordinary conversational walking about2/10. Recognize the assigned markers and exit; no jog, forced technical thigh height, abrupt terminal plant or timed redirect.

P1.variant: Quiet Bilateral Standing — no-step orientation teaching task
P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, minimal effort.2s settle,2s comfortable quiet standing,6s reset. Arms relaxed, knees unlocked; no deliberate lowering, travel or technical knee target.
P1.notes: This observes simple orientation/stop-cue participation only. No travel, marching or upright-running pass follows.

P2.variant: Short Corridor Walk — ordinary walking orientation
P2.effort_load: Bodyweight, ordinary conversational walking about2/10. Recognize the assigned markers and exit; no jog, forced technical thigh height, abrupt terminal plant or timed redirect.
P2.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate18s; separate outside walking return20s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations.

E1.variant: Short Corridor Walk — acceleration/runout/return orientation

S1.variant: Tempo Bodyweight Squat — comfortable bilateral stance/range
S1.effort_load: Bodyweight only;3s lower/1s gentle pause/1s stand, at least5 controlled reps in reserve. Keep the documented OR-01 range when applicable.

S2.variant: Bodyweight Hip Hinge Good Morning — arms crossed at chest
S2.effort_load: Bodyweight;3s hips back/1s stand, at least5 good reps in reserve. Retain the actual comfortable range and arm position.

S3.variant: Incline Push-Up — individually verified stable high support
S3.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s press, at least5 good reps in reserve.90cm is a planning reference only; retain the qualified actual support height and foot position or select a suitable high surface for instruction.
S3.notes: Record actual support height. Older age does not lower the surface or add repetitions.

S4.variant: Ring/TRX Row — verified anchors, about70-degree body angle to floor
S4.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s pull, at least5 good reps in reserve; record actual angle.

S5.variant: Dead Bug Heel Tap — fixed vertical arms, alternating bent-leg heel contact and return
S5.effort_load: Bodyweight, low-load control;2s lower/2s return, natural breathing. Retain a comfortable declared heel target/range without trunk movement.
S5.notes: Tabletop is checked during setup; the first listed heel contact is the counted moving-limb observation. Strength placement is an explicit adaptation of the local preparation profile.

P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
P1.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

P2.variant: Short Corridor Walk — ordinary walking orientation
P2.effort_load: Bodyweight, ordinary conversational walking about2/10. Recognize the assigned markers and exit; no jog, forced technical thigh height, abrupt terminal plant or timed redirect.
P2.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate18s; separate outside walking return20s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations.

E0.effort_load: Bodyweight, ordinary conversational walking about2/10. Recognize the assigned markers and exit; no jog, forced technical thigh height, abrupt terminal plant or timed redirect.
E0.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate45s; separate outside walking return40s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations.

E1.variant: Omitted follow-up — compressed L ends locomotor work after the counted corridor walk
E1.effort_load: No physical effort assigned; observation/recovery only.
E1.notes: Zero physical work: compressed L omits E1, and D-only running routes are unavailable in L.

S1.variant: Tempo Bodyweight Squat — comfortable bilateral stance/range
S1.effort_load: Bodyweight only;3s lower/1s gentle pause/1s stand, at least5 controlled reps in reserve. Keep the documented OR-01 range when applicable.

S2.variant: Bodyweight Hip Hinge Good Morning — arms crossed at chest
S2.effort_load: Bodyweight;3s hips back/1s stand, at least5 good reps in reserve. Retain the actual comfortable range and arm position.

S3.variant: Incline Push-Up — individually verified stable high support
S3.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s press, at least5 good reps in reserve.90cm is a planning reference only; retain the qualified actual support height and foot position or select a suitable high surface for instruction.
S3.notes: Record actual support height. Older age does not lower the surface or add repetitions.

S4.variant: Ring/TRX Row — verified anchors, about70-degree body angle to floor
S4.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s pull, at least5 good reps in reserve; record actual angle.

P1.variant: Quiet Bilateral Standing — no-step orientation teaching task
P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, minimal effort.2s settle,2s comfortable quiet standing,6s reset. Arms relaxed, knees unlocked; no deliberate lowering, travel or technical knee target.
P1.notes: This observes simple orientation/stop-cue participation only. No travel, marching or upright-running pass follows.

P2.variant: Quiet Bilateral Standing — no-step orientation teaching task

E0.variant: Quiet Bilateral Standing — no-step orientation teaching task

E1.variant: Omitted or unavailable opportunity — no physical work
E1.effort_load: No physical effort assigned; observation/recovery only.
E1.notes: Zero physical work: compressed L omits E1, and D-only running routes are unavailable in L.

S1.variant: Tempo Bodyweight Squat — comfortable bilateral stance/range
S1.effort_load: Bodyweight only;3s lower/1s gentle pause/1s stand, at least5 controlled reps in reserve. Keep the documented OR-01 range when applicable.

S2.variant: Bodyweight Hip Hinge Good Morning — arms crossed at chest
S2.effort_load: Bodyweight;3s hips back/1s stand, at least5 good reps in reserve. Retain the actual comfortable range and arm position.

S3.variant: Incline Push-Up — individually verified stable high support
S3.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s press, at least5 good reps in reserve.90cm is a planning reference only; retain the qualified actual support height and foot position or select a suitable high surface for instruction.
S3.notes: Record actual support height. Older age does not lower the surface or add repetitions.

S4.variant: One-Arm Row — opposite hand AND knee on bench
S4.effort_load: One manageable dumbbell: retain a qualified light prior load, or select a very light load for first instruction; at least5 good reps in reserve.1s pull/1s top/2s lower. Record actual kg.
S4.notes: One set includes both sides.10s side change plus10s total pickup/set-down; first listed rep is the observation, never an extra test rep.

S5.variant: Dead Bug Heel Tap — fixed vertical arms, alternating bent-leg heel contact and return
S5.effort_load: Bodyweight, low-load control;2s lower/2s return, natural breathing. Retain a comfortable declared heel target/range without trunk movement.
S5.notes: Tabletop is checked during setup; the first listed heel contact is the counted moving-limb observation. Strength placement is an explicit adaptation of the local preparation profile.

P1.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation
P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
P1.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

P2.variant: Standing Static Short Start — low-intent teaching adaptation
P2.effort_load: Bodyweight; smooth easy intent rising from about2/10 toward3/10, then retain a relaxed comfortable rhythm. No maximal effort, measured speed quota or fly-zone result.
P2.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate15s; separate outside walking return20s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations.

E0.effort_load: Bodyweight, ordinary conversational walking about2/10. Recognize the assigned markers and exit; no jog, forced technical thigh height, abrupt terminal plant or timed redirect.

S3.variant: Incline Push-Up — individually verified stable high support
S3.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s press, at least5 good reps in reserve.90cm is a planning reference only; retain the qualified actual support height and foot position or select a suitable high surface for instruction.
S3.notes: Record actual support height. Older age does not lower the surface or add repetitions.

S4.variant: Ring/TRX Row — verified anchors, about70-degree body angle to floor
S4.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s pull, at least5 good reps in reserve; record actual angle.

S5.notes: Tabletop is checked during setup; the first listed heel contact is the counted moving-limb observation. Strength placement is an explicit adaptation of the local preparation profile.

P1.variant: Quiet Bilateral Standing — no-step orientation teaching task
P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, minimal effort.2s settle,2s comfortable quiet standing,6s reset. Arms relaxed, knees unlocked; no deliberate lowering, travel or technical knee target.
P1.notes: This observes simple orientation/stop-cue participation only. No travel, marching or upright-running pass follows.

P2.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation
P2.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
P2.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

E0.variant: Quiet Bilateral Standing — no-step orientation teaching task
E0.effort_load: Bodyweight, minimal effort.2s settle,2s comfortable quiet standing,6s reset. Arms relaxed, knees unlocked; no deliberate lowering, travel or technical knee target.
E0.notes: This observes simple orientation/stop-cue participation only. No travel, marching or upright-running pass follows.

E1.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation
E1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
E1.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

S1.variant: Tempo Bodyweight Squat — comfortable bilateral stance/range
S1.effort_load: Bodyweight only;3s lower/1s gentle pause/1s stand, at least5 controlled reps in reserve. Keep the documented OR-01 range when applicable.

S2.variant: Bodyweight Hip Hinge Good Morning — arms crossed at chest
S2.effort_load: Bodyweight;3s hips back/1s stand, at least5 good reps in reserve. Retain the actual comfortable range and arm position.

S3.variant: Incline Push-Up — individually verified stable high support
S3.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s press, at least5 good reps in reserve.90cm is a planning reference only; retain the qualified actual support height and foot position or select a suitable high surface for instruction.
S3.notes: Record actual support height. Older age does not lower the surface or add repetitions.

S4.variant: One-Arm Row — opposite hand AND knee on bench
S4.effort_load: One manageable dumbbell: retain a qualified light prior load, or select a very light load for first instruction; at least5 good reps in reserve.1s pull/1s top/2s lower. Record actual kg.
S4.notes: One set includes both sides.10s side change plus10s total pickup/set-down; first listed rep is the observation, never an extra test rep.

S5.variant: 90/90 Breathing with Reach — lower-leg-supported-bilateral-reach
S5.effort_load: Very low; comfortable2s in/3s out, no holds or forced depth; calves/heels fully supported, no heel pull/hip lift.

P1.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation
P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
P1.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

P2.variant: Standing Static Short Start — low-intent teaching adaptation
P2.effort_load: Bodyweight; smooth easy intent rising from about2/10 toward3/10, then retain a relaxed comfortable rhythm. No maximal effort, measured speed quota or fly-zone result.
P2.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate15s; separate outside walking return20s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations.

E0.effort_load: Bodyweight, ordinary conversational walking about2/10. Recognize the assigned markers and exit; no jog, forced technical thigh height, abrupt terminal plant or timed redirect.
E0.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate45s; separate outside walking return40s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations.

E1.variant: Easy Build and Upright Rhythm Run — explicitly authored teaching adaptation
E1.effort_load: Bodyweight; smooth easy intent rising from about2/10 toward3/10, then retain a relaxed comfortable rhythm. No maximal effort, measured speed quota or fly-zone result.
E1.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate25s; separate outside walking return40s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations.

S1.variant: Tempo Bodyweight Squat — comfortable bilateral stance/range
S1.effort_load: Bodyweight only;3s lower/1s gentle pause/1s stand, at least5 controlled reps in reserve. Keep the documented OR-01 range when applicable.

S2.variant: Bodyweight Hip Hinge Good Morning — arms crossed at chest
S2.effort_load: Bodyweight;3s hips back/1s stand, at least5 good reps in reserve. Retain the actual comfortable range and arm position.

S3.variant: Incline Push-Up — individually verified stable high support
S3.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s press, at least5 good reps in reserve.90cm is a planning reference only; retain the qualified actual support height and foot position or select a suitable high surface for instruction.
S3.notes: Record actual support height. Older age does not lower the surface or add repetitions.

S4.variant: Ring/TRX Row — verified anchors, about70-degree body angle to floor
S4.effort_load: Bodyweight;2s lower/1s pull, at least5 good reps in reserve; record actual angle.

S5.variant: Dead Bug Heel Tap — fixed vertical arms, alternating bent-leg heel contact and return
S5.effort_load: Bodyweight, low-load control;2s lower/2s return, natural breathing. Retain a comfortable declared heel target/range without trunk movement.
S5.notes: Tabletop is checked during setup; the first listed heel contact is the counted moving-limb observation. Strength placement is an explicit adaptation of the local preparation profile.
